subject.title: [Feature]: Pre-reset agentic memory flush — /new and daily reset should get the same memory flush as compaction

question: Should OpenClaw add a silent agentic pre-reset memory flush for manual, daily, idle, and gateway reset paths, and what contract should govern timing, defaults, tools, provider routing, privacy, and plugin-hook interaction?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds silent model/tool execution and durable memory writes at reset boundaries, which requires product and security intent before implementation.

options.title: Design one reset-memory lifecycle
options.body: Define a bounded policy for explicit `/new`/`/reset`, daily/idle rollover, and gateway resets, including timeout, cancellation, delivery suppression, sandbox/tool allow, provider/auth routing, docs, and regression coverage.

options.title: Start default-off and narrow
options.body: Add an opt-in manual or daily reset flush first, then expand after proving UX, provider, and privacy behavior.

options.title: Reject agentic reset flushing
options.body: Rely on mechanical session-memory hooks, existing startup context, external memory plugins such as world-model-mcp, and separate restore/continuity work instead of adding a core silent turn.

recommendation.title: Design one reset-memory lifecycle
recommendation.body: Define a bounded policy for explicit `/new`/`/reset`, daily/idle rollover, and gateway resets, including timeout, cancellation, delivery suppression, sandbox/tool allow, provider/auth routing, docs, and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the pre-compaction memory flush and daily reset policy that this design needs to reconcile.
